note: Designs are pre/post, ABAB, parity holdout or matched page groups; see 31-EXPERIMENTS.md §2.

experiments.name: Social sign-in above the email form
experiments.hypothesis: Putting Google, Discord and Battle.net (and Steam once D-015 ships) above the password form raises completion, because social sign-up skips Turnstile, the five-rule password and the inbox wait [R11 §1.3].
experiments.audience: All visitors to /register (phone layout first: 1,487 phone vs 184 desktop requests [R11]).
experiments.change: RegisterClient.tsx: full-width social buttons on top, 'or with email' form below (C44 page rewrite, R-02 in 15-REGISTRATION).
experiments.metric: registration_complete ÷ /register sessions (first-party), split by method
experiments.expected_learning: Whether friction (the gates) or motivation (the offer) is what stops sign-ups.
experiments.success_threshold: Post-window completion rate ≥ 1.5× the 14-day pre-window AND ≥ 60% of completions via a social method, with ≥ 15 completions in the post window.

experiments.name: Honest register panel (trust fix)
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing '15K+ MEMBERS · 50K+ GAMES' and the false read-XP perk with the homepage's four mechanisms and an API-fed game count does not reduce completion.
experiments.change: D-001 copy change on /register and /login; no other change in the same fortnight.
experiments.metric: registration_complete ÷ /register sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Shows that removing false social proof costs nothing measurable; the change ships regardless because it is a correctness fix.
experiments.success_threshold: Non-inferiority: post-window completion rate ≥ 0.8× the pre-window rate. A lower result is recorded, not reverted.

experiments.name: Steam as a sign-in method
experiments.hypothesis: A 'Sign in through Steam' button produces A2 Shelved members at ≥ 2× the rate of email sign-ups, because the library imports on the first click [R11 §5].
experiments.audience: /register visitors and the onboarding wizard; S2 Multi-platform Collectors, S3 PC Tinkerers.
experiments.change: D-015 Steam OpenID login creating the account from the SteamID64 and starting the import job; email asked for later (X-016).
experiments.metric: registration_complete (method=steam); library_connected within 7 days by method
experiments.expected_learning: Whether 'the library is the sign-up' is TechPlay's best acquisition argument.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 10 Steam sign-ups in 28 days AND their 7-day A2 rate ≥ 2× the email-method A2 rate in the same window.

experiments.name: Return new members to where they started
experiments.hypothesis: Returning a new member to the page they came from (comment box, game page, giveaway) raises the share who act within the first hour.
experiments.audience: Registrants arriving from comments, game pages, giveaways (from=comments|game|giveaway).
experiments.change: D-014 honours ?redirect= for social sign-ups and verified email sign-ups; D-016 resumes the action.
experiments.metric: Share of registration_complete followed by comment_created, shelf_add or reminder_set within 60 minutes
experiments.expected_learning: How much intent is lost at the registration hop today.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 40% of redirected registrants act within 60 minutes (pre-period share from a users/comments/user_games timestamp query), minimum 10 registrants.

experiments.name: Guest 'Remind me' on game and calendar pages
experiments.hypothesis: Game pages are the largest sign-up surface (56,355 URLs indexed [R03]); a guest 'Remind me' that opens a sign-up modal and returns to the game converts better than today's login link.
experiments.audience: Guests on unreleased game pages, /calendar and /calendar/[slug].
experiments.change: D-016 modal ('Tell me when {game} is out. Free account, one click with Google or Discord.'), C45.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (from=game|calendar); reminder_set in the first session
experiments.expected_learning: Whether release intent is a stronger sign-up reason than 'start your library'.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 20 registrations with from=game or from=calendar in 28 days AND ≥ 70% of them have reminder_set in the same session.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Game-specific article-end prompt
experiments.hypothesis: On articles with a game_id, 'Add {game} to your shelf' earns more clicks than the generic account panel.
experiments.audience: Guests reading articles that carry articles.game_id.
experiments.change: JoinPrompt variant inside the D-010 article-end block; alternate generic and game variants by ISO week (ABAB).
experiments.metric: cta_click (cta_id=article-end-join-generic vs article-end-join-game) per 1,000 article sessions; registration_complete from=article-game
experiments.expected_learning: Whether specificity beats a general pitch on the surface with the most readers.
experiments.success_threshold: Game variant click rate ≥ 1.3× generic in both of its weeks, with ≥ 30 clicks in total.

experiments.name: Verify-email page that says what already works
experiments.hypothesis: Explaining what works before verification (shelf, import) and what verification unlocks (comments, giveaways, digest) raises 72-hour verification.
experiments.change: Copy change on /verify-email (R-05 in 15-REGISTRATION): one list of 'works now', one of 'after you click the link'.
experiments.metric: email_verified within 72 h ÷ registration_complete (method=email); weekly prune count
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the inbox gate loses people through confusion or through a missing mail.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 90% verify within 72 h (last reading: 50 of 55 confirmed, undated window [R12]) AND prune count does not rise.

experiments.name: Newsletter verify page offers an account
experiments.hypothesis: The moment after double opt-in is warm; a pre-filled 'make it an account' with Google one-tap converts ≥ 10% of new verified subscribers.
experiments.audience: People landing on /newsletter/verify after clicking the confirmation link.
experiments.change: Panel on app/newsletter/verify/page.tsx: 'You're on the list. Want your games in one place too?' with Google/Discord buttons and email pre-filled.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (from=newsletter-verify) ÷ newsletter_verified
experiments.expected_learning: Whether newsletter and account are one audience or two.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 10% of newly verified subscribers register within 10 minutes, measured over ≥ 50 verifications.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Leaderboard empty state becomes an invitation
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing 'Nobody has moved yet this week' with 'Be the first this week: connect Steam and your completions count' turns an empty page into a sign-up path.
experiments.change: Copy and CTA on the empty state (D-029 hides zero-value modules elsewhere).
experiments.metric: cta_click (cta_id=leaderboard-empty-connect); registration_complete (from=leaderboard)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether competitive framing works at a population of 60.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 5 registrations with from=leaderboard in 28 days (pre-period assumed 0; nothing measured it).
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Buffy replies with a one-click account link
experiments.hypothesis: Unlinked Discord members who use /daily, /profile or /library register at ≥ 20% when the bot answers with a Discord OAuth link that lands on the shelf [R11 row 20].
experiments.audience: Discord members with no linked TechPlay account who run a member command.
experiments.change: Bot reply footer: 'This works better with your library behind it. Link in one click:' → Discord OAuth → /profile shelf.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (method=discord, from=discord) ÷ distinct unlinked command users
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the Discord room is the highest-intent acquisition pool TechPlay has.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 20% of unlinked members who trigger a command register within 14 days, minimum 10 distinct members.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Wizard order: connect Steam first vs pick games first
experiments.hypothesis: Opening the onboarding wizard on 'connect Steam' produces more A2 members than opening on 'pick games', because import fills the shelf in one step.
experiments.change: Alternate the first wizard step by ISO week (ABAB).
experiments.metric: wizard_shown → library_connected or wizard_pick_done; A2 within 7 days
experiments.expected_learning: Which first step carries more members over the A2 line.
experiments.success_threshold: Winning order's 7-day A2 rate ≥ 1.3× the other across both of its weeks, with ≥ 15 wizard_shown per arm; otherwise extend by 2 weeks and call it inconclusive.

experiments.name: Founding 100 framing
experiments.hypothesis: Telling registrants that the first 100 members who connect a platform or shelve three games get the Founder badge raises the A2 rate.
experiments.audience: All new members from launch of C68.
experiments.change: Extend campaign:founders from 50 (≥5 games) to 100 with the A2 rule; show a live 'N of 100 claimed' count from the API on /register and in the wizard.
experiments.metric: A2 within 7 days of registration_complete; badges awarded
experiments.expected_learning: Whether scarcity that is true moves activation without inflating anything.
experiments.success_threshold: 7-day A2 rate ≥ 1.5× the 21-day pre-window AND ≥ 25 badges awarded by 31 Oct. The count shown must be live; no placeholder.

experiments.name: Library-worth card straight after import
experiments.hypothesis: Showing 'Your Steam library: N games, $X at today's prices' right after import increases sharing and 7-day return.
experiments.audience: Members completing a Steam import (US Steam prices only [R01]).
experiments.change: Card on the import-complete screen with Save/Share (D-024 share card route).
experiments.metric: share_card_generated (type=library-worth) ÷ library_connected (platform=steam); A3 within 7 days
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a number about their own library is the share trigger TOOL-03 scored it as [R21].
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 15% of Steam importers generate a card AND ≥ 3 registrations arrive through card links (from=share-card) in 28 days.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Welcome email 2: link your library
experiments.hypothesis: A day-2 email ('Your shelf is empty. Steam takes 30 seconds.') raises A2 among members who have not activated.
experiments.audience: Non-activated new members; alternate by user id parity (treated vs holdout).
experiments.change: Email 2 of the C42 welcome sequence; holdout receives nothing on day 2.
experiments.metric: library_connected within 7 days, treated vs holdout
experiments.expected_learning: Whether email can do activation work the bell cannot.
experiments.success_threshold: Treated A2 rate ≥ holdout + 10 percentage points with ≥ 30 members per arm; below 30 per arm the result is read as directional only.

experiments.name: Three-item checklist instead of seven
experiments.hypothesis: Cutting ProfileChecklist from seven items to three (connect a platform, add three games, set one reminder) raises completion of those three.
experiments.change: ProfileChecklist.tsx shows three items; the other four move to a 'later' list.
experiments.metric: Share of new members with library_connected or 3× shelf_add AND reminder_set within 7 days
experiments.expected_learning: Whether choice overload is part of the activation gap (3 of 55 added a game [R12]).
experiments.success_threshold: Share completing all three ≥ 2× the share who did the same three things in the 28-day pre-window.

experiments.name: Ask Steam-only accounts for email at the reminder
experiments.hypothesis: Asking 'Where should we send the release reminder?' at the moment of reminder_set gets an email from ≥ 50% of Steam-only accounts [R11 §5].
experiments.audience: Accounts created through Steam sign-in with no email.
experiments.change: Inline email field in the reminder confirmation; email verified by link.
experiments.metric: Email attached ÷ Steam-only accounts that set a reminder
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Steam sign-in accounts can become reachable without a gate.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 50% attach and verify an email, minimum 10 Steam-only reminder setters.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Gamer DNA card at ten shelf items
experiments.hypothesis: Prompting the Gamer DNA share card once a member reaches ten shelf items produces shares that bring registrations.
experiments.change: One-time prompt with the D-024 card and Save/Share.
experiments.metric: share_card_generated (type=gamer-dna); registration_complete (from=share-card)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether identity cards travel for TechPlay the way recaps do elsewhere [R11 §2.5].
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 20% of eligible members generate a card AND ≥ 5 registrations via card links in 28 days.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Backlog Advisor guest mode
experiments.hypothesis: Letting guests type five games and get a pick, then offering 'import your backlog instead of typing it', converts better than the sign-in wall.
experiments.change: D-037 guest mode; result screen ends with Steam/Google sign-up that imports.
experiments.metric: tool_run (tool=backlog, guest); registration_complete (from=advisor)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a useful answer before sign-up beats a promise of one.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 100 guest runs AND ≥ 5% of runs followed by registration within the session.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Homepage newsletter block
experiments.hypothesis: A homepage capture block for The Save File converts at least 3 per 1,000 homepage sessions; today there is no homepage capture [R20].
experiments.audience: Homepage visitors, signed out and signed in.
experiments.change: D-012 block under the hero: 'The Save File. Fridays. The week's releases, one fix, one number. No spam, one-click unsubscribe.'
experiments.metric: newsletter_signup (placement=home) per 1,000 homepage sessions; newsletter_verified ÷ newsletter_signup
experiments.expected_learning: The capture rate of the most-seen page, to size every other placement against.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 3 signups per 1,000 homepage sessions AND ≥ 70% verify within 72 h.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Article end: newsletter first vs account first
experiments.hypothesis: One ordering of the D-010 end block (newsletter field above the account prompt, or the reverse) produces more total owned-audience actions.
experiments.change: Alternate order by ISO week (ABAB); copy identical.
experiments.metric: (newsletter_signup + registration_complete) per 1,000 article sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Which ask a reader at the end of a news story will accept.
experiments.success_threshold: Winning order ≥ 1.25× the combined rate in both of its weeks, with ≥ 40 combined actions in total.

experiments.name: /newsletter landing with a real sample issue
experiments.hypothesis: Showing the latest issue (web archive of F21) on /newsletter raises conversion of that page.
experiments.audience: Visitors to /newsletter (new) from social, Discord and the footer.
experiments.change: Embed the most recent issue under the form from the first issue onward; before that, the promise only.
experiments.metric: newsletter_signup ÷ /newsletter sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Whether proof of the product beats a description of it.
experiments.success_threshold: Post-window rate ≥ 1.3× pre-window with ≥ 200 landing sessions across both windows.

experiments.name: Specific subject lines vs numbered ones
experiments.hypothesis: Subject lines naming the week's concrete items ('GTA VI pre-load date, 6 releases, 1 fix') get more clicks than numbered ones ('The Save File #3').
experiments.change: Alternate style by issue over eight issues.
experiments.metric: Unique clicks ÷ delivered per issue (opens are a floor only [R20])
experiments.expected_learning: Which subject style drives the click, the only trusted email metric.
experiments.success_threshold: Specific style click rate ≥ 1.2× numbered across 4 issues each, with unsubscribe ≤ 0.5% on every send.

experiments.name: Send time: Friday 08:00 vs 16:00 CET
experiments.hypothesis: The Save File sent Friday 08:00 CET gets more 48-hour clicks than Friday 16:00 CET (the digest's current slot).
experiments.change: Alternate send time by week for eight weeks.
experiments.metric: Unique clicks within 48 h ÷ delivered
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the US-heavy audience (about 35% of traffic [R16]) changes the best slot.
experiments.success_threshold: One slot wins by ≥ 20% relative in at least 3 of 4 weekly pairs; otherwise keep 16:00.

experiments.name: GTA 6 briefing with a dated promise
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing 'Join thousands of fans' with a dated promise ('One email a week until 19 Nov, daily in launch week. Confirmed facts, sources linked.') raises capture on /gta6.
experiments.change: Gta6NewsletterCTA.tsx copy (D-001) and a gta6 tag on the subscriber row (D-012).
experiments.metric: newsletter_signup (placement=gta6) per 1,000 /gta6 sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a specific, time-bound promise outperforms vague social proof.
experiments.success_threshold: Post-window rate ≥ 1.5× the pre-window with ≥ 30 signups in the post window.

experiments.name: Email-only release alert for guests
experiments.hypothesis: An email-only 'tell me when it's out' on unreleased game pages captures more guests than the account-only reminder, and ≥ 20% of those later register.
experiments.change: Alternate weeks: account modal (X-005) vs email-only alert field; run after X-005 has 28 days of data.
experiments.metric: newsletter_signup (placement=game-page) + reminder by email per 1,000 game sessions; registration_complete within 30 days
experiments.expected_learning: Whether asking for less (an address) beats asking for an account at the release moment.
experiments.success_threshold: Email-only capture ≥ 2× the account variant per 1,000 game sessions AND ≥ 20% of email-only signups register within 30 days.

experiments.name: Newsletter line in Buffy's welcome
experiments.hypothesis: One line with the /newsletter link in the Discord welcome embed converts ≥ 5% of new joiners to subscribers.
experiments.change: BuffyService welcome embed adds: 'Fridays: The Save File, the week in one email.' with utm_source=discord&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=c35-discord-rebuild.
experiments.metric: newsletter_signup with utm_source=discord ÷ discord_join
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Discord and email audiences overlap or feed each other.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 5% of joiners subscribe within 28 days, minimum 40 joins.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Discord Onboarding questions
experiments.hypothesis: Three Onboarding questions (platforms, games followed, which pings) raise the share of joiners who post within seven days.
experiments.change: C35 rebuild: Onboarding with three questions assigning roles and channels.
experiments.metric: Joiners with ≥ 1 message within 7 days ÷ joiners (bot count)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the first minute in the server decides whether people stay.
experiments.success_threshold: Rate ≥ 1.5× the 21-day pre-window with ≥ 30 joiners in the post window.

experiments.name: End-of-article Discord line vs sidebar widget
experiments.hypothesis: An end-of-article Discord line gets more clicks per 1,000 article sessions than the desktop-only sidebar widget, because the phone layout is the real one [R11].
experiments.change: D-010 end block gains a Discord line with its own invite code; the sidebar widget gets a second code.
experiments.metric: discord_click (placement=article-end vs article-sidebar); discord_join by invite code
experiments.expected_learning: Where Discord asks work on a phone-first site.
experiments.success_threshold: Article-end ≥ 2× sidebar clicks per 1,000 sessions AND joins by code point the same way.

experiments.name: Invite copy that names a dated event
experiments.hypothesis: Invites naming a dated event ('Game Club night this Thursday, 20:00 CET: Control Resonant') convert better than 'Join our Discord'.
experiments.change: Two invite codes, two copies, alternated across posts for four weeks.
experiments.metric: discord_join per 100 discord_click, per invite code
experiments.expected_learning: Whether events are the reason to join [R13].
experiments.success_threshold: Event copy ≥ 1.5× joins per 100 clicks with ≥ 20 joins in total.

experiments.name: 'What Are You Playing?' on site and Discord together
experiments.hypothesis: Running F11 as one prompt on Discord and the forum, cross-linked, lifts distinct participants compared with Discord alone.
experiments.audience: Discord members, forum readers, social followers.
experiments.change: C37 weekly thread posted Monday in Discord and /forum with links both ways; first four weeks Discord-only, next four both.
experiments.metric: Distinct participants per week (Discord authors + forum repliers); comment_created on the forum thread
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the forum can borrow Discord's activity instead of competing with it.
experiments.success_threshold: Distinct participants in weeks 5–8 ≥ 1.3× weeks 1–4 AND the forum thread averages ≥ 5 replies.

experiments.name: Recruiter role for member invites
experiments.hypothesis: A 'Recruiter' role for members who bring three joiners through their own invite codes produces ≥ 15% of joins.
experiments.change: C36: members create personal invites; the bot credits joins by code (D-011); role at 3 joins.
experiments.metric: Share of discord_join attributed to member-created codes
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the community can grow itself at this size.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 15% of joins from member codes AND zero raid or spam incidents linked to the scheme.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Buffy's daily On This Day post
experiments.hypothesis: A daily automated anniversary post (F06) raises distinct daily posters in #general.
experiments.change: C65: Buffy posts one anniversary from /games/on-this-day at a fixed time.
experiments.metric: Distinct authors per day in #general (bot count; Server Insights needs 500+ members [R13])
experiments.expected_learning: Whether automated prompts start conversations or become wallpaper.
experiments.success_threshold: Distinct daily posters +25% vs the 14-day pre-window, with no rise in moderation actions.

experiments.name: Link-your-account line in the welcome
experiments.hypothesis: A welcome message asking members to link their TechPlay account (XP carries over) raises linked members.
experiments.change: Welcome embed line with the /link command and the site link.
experiments.metric: Joiners with a linked account within 14 days (users.discord_id with discord_guild_member = true)
experiments.expected_learning: How much of the Discord audience will cross to the site.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 15% of joiners link within 14 days.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Shrink the indexable game set
experiments.hypothesis: Noindexing game pages without an original signal shifts Googlebot's ~290 daily fetches toward articles and hubs and speeds article indexing [R03 §9].
experiments.change: D-021: Game::indexable() requires an original signal; the long tail stays crawlable and linked but noindex.
experiments.metric: GSC crawl stats (requests by page type), indexed articles, organic clicks
experiments.expected_learning: Whether index quality, not access, is what holds search back.
experiments.success_threshold: Articles+hubs share of Googlebot requests ≥ 2× the pre-window AND ≥ 90% of articles published after the change indexed within 7 days, with organic clicks not falling below the pre-window.

experiments.name: Contextual links in every article
experiments.hypothesis: Three to five contextual links per article (game page, calendar, tool) raise pages per session from article landings.
experiments.change: D-010 contextual links and related module; ED adds links at publish.
experiments.metric: Pages per session for sessions landing on an article (first-party, sessions with sid); cta_click
experiments.expected_learning: Whether articles can feed the database and tools.
experiments.success_threshold: Pages per session from article landings +15% vs the 28-day pre-window.

experiments.name: Review titles that carry a verdict
experiments.hypothesis: 'Crimson Desert review: [verdict in five words] (PS5, PC)' gets a higher Search CTR than 'Crimson Desert - review' [R03 §10].
experiments.change: Retitle the 10 reviews with most impressions; 10 comparable reviews untouched as control.
experiments.metric: GSC CTR, treated vs control, 28 days before and after (difference-in-differences)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether title quality is part of the invisibility of reviews.
experiments.success_threshold: Treated CTR change ≥ 30% relative above the control group's change, with ≥ 500 impressions per group.

experiments.name: PC fix guides vs news for search clicks
experiments.hypothesis: P2 fix guides earn search clicks faster than news because page one has no gaming outlet for them [R09].
experiments.change: C60 PC Fix Hub: one F07 guide a week from 12 Oct.
experiments.metric: GSC clicks per page at day 28, fix guides vs news published the same weeks
experiments.expected_learning: Where ED hours earn the most durable traffic.
experiments.success_threshold: Median fix guide ≥ 3× median news article clicks at day 28, with ≥ 4 guides.
experiments.design: concurrent comparison (guides vs news, same weeks)

experiments.name: Series order pages
experiments.hypothesis: F09 'In Order' pages reach page one for '[series] games in order' within six weeks.
experiments.change: C63: one series page each Saturday from 3 Oct.
experiments.metric: GSC average position and clicks for each page's main query
experiments.expected_learning: Whether evergreen order guides are winnable for a small site.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 3 of the first 6 pages at average position ≤ 10 for their main query by day 42.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: 'Where can I play it' blocks on 200 game pages
experiments.hypothesis: A verified 'where to play' block (platforms, subscriptions, Switch 2 edition) on 200 high-demand game pages lifts impressions against 200 matched pages without it [R09 EA-085].
experiments.change: F08 template filled by ED on 200 pages; 200 matched pages as control.
experiments.metric: GSC impressions and clicks per page group
experiments.expected_learning: Whether original structured answers make database pages worth indexing.
experiments.success_threshold: Treated group impressions +50% relative to the control group's change over the same window.

experiments.name: A paragraph of our own on game pages
experiments.hypothesis: Two sentences of TechPlay context plus linked news or review turns boilerplate game pages into indexable ones [R02 fix 12].
experiments.audience: Game pages with any TechPlay signal (1,967 of 295,024 [R03]).
experiments.change: 150 treated pages get the paragraph; 150 matched pages do not.
experiments.metric: Indexed status (URL Inspection sample) and impressions per group
experiments.expected_learning: The editorial cost of making a game page 'ours'.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 25% more treated pages indexed than control pages at day 42.

experiments.name: One home for GTA 6 in search
experiments.hypothesis: Re-pointing GTA 6 news to /games/grand-theft-auto-vi and linking hub, game page and calendar makes one URL rank for GTA queries [R17].
experiments.change: D-005 relation fix, D-017 server-rendered hub counters and H1, internal links.
experiments.metric: GSC impressions for queries containing 'gta 6' or 'gta vi' on /gta6* and the game page
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the hub can compete at all before launch week.
experiments.success_threshold: Impressions ×3 vs the 28-day pre-window AND at least one page at average position ≤ 20 for a 'gta 6 …' query by 19 Nov.

experiments.name: Google News clean-up plus original pieces
experiments.hypothesis: Stopping game pages from appearing as news and publishing original data pieces gets TechPlay articles into Google News [R03 §6].
experiments.change: D-022 (datePublished on game pages); C20 and C22 as original reporting.
experiments.metric: Monthly probe of 16 own-topic Google News RSS searches (R03 method); GSC News tab if shown
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Google News is reachable this quarter.
experiments.success_threshold: By 31 Oct: zero game pages in the site: News feed. By 30 Nov: ≥ 2 of 16 probes return a TechPlay article.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: RSS repair feeding Flipboard and Mastodon
experiments.hypothesis: Fixing RSS and piping it to Flipboard and Mastodon produces referral sessions for under an hour a week.
experiments.change: D-003; SC connects the feed once.
experiments.metric: Sessions by referrer_host (flipboard.com, Mastodon instance hosts)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether low-priority channels pay for their setup.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 20 sessions/week by week 6 at ≤ 1 h/week effort; otherwise stop maintaining.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Concrete headlines vs question headlines
experiments.hypothesis: Headlines that put the answer in the title ('Gears of War: E-Day release time in every time zone') earn more Discover clicks than question headlines.
experiments.change: Alternate style by publishing day for four weeks on pillar news.
experiments.metric: Discover clicks per article in the first 72 h (GSC Discover report)
experiments.expected_learning: Which headline style Discover rewards for TechPlay after the Feb 2026 update [R07].
experiments.success_threshold: Concrete style median ≥ 1.5× question style with ≥ 20 articles per style. Void if the Discover report shows no data.

experiments.name: Original 1200px images vs store key art
experiments.hypothesis: Original large images (annotated screenshots, data cards) get a higher Discover CTR than publisher key art.
experiments.change: DS templates; alternate by article; all images ≥ 1200px wide and ≤ 300 KB.
experiments.metric: Discover CTR per article
experiments.expected_learning: Whether image originality is worth DS hours.
experiments.success_threshold: Original-image CTR ≥ 1.25× key-art CTR with ≥ 15 articles per arm.

experiments.name: Pillar concentration
experiments.hypothesis: Putting ≥ 70% of news into pillars P1–P3 for six weeks (and dropping general tech and phones) raises Discover impressions through topic expertise [R07, R08].
experiments.change: EIC editorial rule for six weeks; ED tags each article with its pillar.
experiments.metric: Discover impressions per week; total Google clicks
experiments.expected_learning: Whether focus beats volume for a two-author newsroom.
experiments.success_threshold: Weekly Discover impressions in weeks 4–6 ≥ 2× the pre-window mean, with total Google clicks not lower.

experiments.name: Author expertise boxes on guides
experiments.hypothesis: A short author box (what they play, test hardware, how it was tested) on P2 and P3 guides improves Discover and Search performance.
experiments.change: Box on 8 guides; 8 comparable guides later.
experiments.metric: Clicks per guide over 42 days, treated vs control
experiments.expected_learning: Whether visible expertise signals move a small site.
experiments.success_threshold: Treated guides ≥ 1.2× control clicks.

experiments.name: Publishing time for US stories
experiments.hypothesis: US-relevant stories published 13:00–15:00 CET (US morning) earn more Discover clicks in 48 h than those published at 08:00 CET.
experiments.change: Alternate publish slot by day for four weeks.
experiments.metric: Discover clicks in the first 48 h
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the Sarajevo schedule costs US reach.
experiments.success_threshold: US-slot median ≥ 1.3× morning-slot median with ≥ 12 stories per slot.

experiments.name: Stories framed on TechPlay's own data
experiments.hypothesis: News framed around a figure from TechPlay's calendar or database gets more Discover clicks than a rewrite of the same news.
experiments.change: ED adds one database figure (with source line) as the news hook, F04 style.
experiments.metric: Discover clicks per article, data-framed vs rewrite
experiments.expected_learning: Whether owned data is the originality Discover wants.
experiments.success_threshold: Data-framed median ≥ 2× rewrites with ≥ 8 data-framed pieces.

experiments.name: Out This Week: carousel vs single image on Instagram
experiments.hypothesis: An F01 carousel earns more saves per 1,000 reach than a single image of the same list.
experiments.change: Alternate format by week for six weeks; same DS template family.
experiments.metric: Saves + shares per 1,000 reach (platform analytics); link-sticker sessions with utm_content f01-*
experiments.expected_learning: Which format justifies DS time on the weekly anchor.
experiments.success_threshold: Carousel ≥ 1.5× saves per 1,000 reach across 3 weeks each.

experiments.name: GTA countdown Stories: fact card vs poll sticker
experiments.hypothesis: An F02 Story with a poll sticker gets more interactions per viewer than a fact card alone.
experiments.change: Alternate by day for 14 days.
experiments.metric: Replies + sticker taps per 100 viewers; link taps with utm_content f02-dayNN-story
experiments.expected_learning: Which Story mechanic to use for the remaining countdown.
experiments.success_threshold: Winner ≥ 1.3× interactions per 100 viewers; adopt it for the rest of C06.

experiments.name: X: thread vs single post for Out This Week
experiments.hypothesis: A single post with the carousel image and one link sends more sessions than a thread.
experiments.change: Alternate by week for four weeks.
experiments.metric: Sessions with utm_source=x and utm_content f01-*
experiments.expected_learning: The cheapest X format that still sends readers.
experiments.success_threshold: Winner ≥ 1.5× sessions per post.

experiments.name: Reddit: answer first, link second
experiments.hypothesis: Answers that solve the question in the thread and link only when a TechPlay page adds data or a tool keep standing positive and still send readers [R13].
experiments.change: C47 rules: 9 of 10 contributions without a link; links carry utm_medium=community and utm_term=<subreddit>.
experiments.metric: Removals and bans; median comment score; sessions with utm_source=reddit
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Reddit can be a steady source without burning the account.
experiments.success_threshold: Zero removals or bans, median score ≥ 2, and ≥ 30 sessions/week by week 8.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Threads and Bluesky cross-posts of The Number
experiments.hypothesis: Cross-posting F04 to Threads and Bluesky costs under an hour a week and returns ≥ 10 sessions a week on each.
experiments.change: SC cross-posts F04 three times a week.
experiments.metric: Sessions with utm_source=threads / bluesky; SC minutes logged
experiments.expected_learning: Keep-or-kill for two experimental channels.
experiments.success_threshold: Each platform ≥ 10 sessions/week in weeks 4–6 at ≤ 1 h/week; otherwise stop that platform.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Facebook: Page vs relevant Groups for Hidden Gem
experiments.hypothesis: F05 shared in relevant Facebook Groups (with admin permission) sends more readers than the Page alone.
experiments.change: Alternate Page-only and Group shares by week for six weeks.
experiments.metric: Sessions with utm_source=facebook, utm_content f05-*
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Facebook's reach lives in Groups for TechPlay.
experiments.success_threshold: Group weeks ≥ 3× Page-only weeks in sessions, with zero removals.

experiments.name: LinkedIn Studio Watch
experiments.hypothesis: One F17 post a week on LinkedIn brings industry readers and press contacts.
experiments.change: EIC posts F17 each Thursday with the /data/studios-closed-2026 tracker.
experiments.metric: Sessions with utm_source=linkedin; inbound industry contacts logged
experiments.expected_learning: Whether LinkedIn earns its slot for PR.
experiments.success_threshold: Median ≥ 15 sessions per post AND ≥ 2 inbound industry contacts by 31 Dec.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Library Card member spotlight
experiments.hypothesis: An opt-in member spotlight (F19) makes other readers start their own library.
experiments.change: SC posts one consenting member's Gamer DNA card each Friday.
experiments.metric: registration_start and registration_complete with utm_content f19-*
experiments.expected_learning: Whether members' own artefacts sell accounts better than our copy.
experiments.success_threshold: Median ≥ 3 registrations per spotlight over 6 spotlights, with written consent logged for every member featured.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Steam Curator page referrals
experiments.hypothesis: A Steam Curator page with short verdicts linking to TechPlay reviews brings followers and referral sessions.
experiments.change: C69 launch with 20 recommendations, 2 new per week.
experiments.metric: Curator followers; sessions with utm_source=steam
experiments.expected_learning: Whether Steam is a distribution channel for Verdict.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 50 curator followers and ≥ 10 sessions/week by 31 Dec.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Hook: number on screen vs talking-head intro
experiments.hypothesis: F01 videos that open on an on-screen date or number hold viewers longer than those opening on a presenter line.
experiments.change: Alternate hook style across 8 F01 videos.
experiments.metric: Average percentage viewed; 3-second hold (platform analytics)
experiments.expected_learning: The hook template for the whole C49 system.
experiments.success_threshold: Winning hook ≥ 1.2× average percentage viewed across 4 videos each.

experiments.name: One production, four platforms
experiments.hypothesis: Posting the same vertical file to TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and Facebook Reels shows which one or two platforms deserve the time.
experiments.change: C49 posts identical files; SC records views, follows and link sessions per platform.
experiments.metric: Views at 7 days, follows per 1,000 views, utm sessions per 1,000 views, per platform
experiments.expected_learning: Where video attention should go in Q1 2027.
experiments.success_threshold: Keep platforms at ≥ 2× the median of the others on follows per 1,000 views; drop any platform below one quarter of the best after 6 weeks.

experiments.name: Fix It Friday shorts with a guide link
experiments.hypothesis: F07 shorts send readers to the full guide through the description or pinned-comment link.
experiments.audience: S3 PC Tinkerers on YouTube and TikTok.
experiments.change: Every F07 short links /guides/pc-fixes/<guide> with utm_content f07-short-<slug>.
experiments.metric: Sessions per 1,000 views with utm_content f07-*
experiments.expected_learning: Whether video can feed the pillar that search rewards.
experiments.success_threshold: Median ≥ 2 sessions per 1,000 views.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Out This Week length: 20–30 s vs 45–60 s
experiments.hypothesis: Shorter F01 videos have higher completion without losing views.
experiments.change: Alternate length by week for six weeks.
experiments.metric: Completion rate and views at 7 days
experiments.expected_learning: The default length for the weekly anchor.
experiments.success_threshold: Short version completion ≥ 1.3× with views not lower than 0.8× the long version.

experiments.name: YouTube long-form pilot
experiments.hypothesis: One long video ('Every GTA game in order before VI', 12 Nov) earns more subscribers per production hour than Shorts.
experiments.audience: YouTube viewers searching GTA order before launch.
experiments.change: C50 pilot; EIC scripts, SC edits.
experiments.metric: Subscribers gained per production hour at day 28; views at day 28; utm sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Whether long-form belongs in Q1 2027 plans.
experiments.success_threshold: Subscribers per production hour ≥ 2× the Shorts figure over the same 28 days.

experiments.name: WoW Analyzer 15-second demo
experiments.hypothesis: A screen recording of an Analyzer result drives tool runs from YouTube and TikTok.
experiments.change: One organic demo per month (F15), linked with utm_campaign=c13-wow-readiness.
experiments.metric: tool_run (tool=wow) with utm_campaign c13-*
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the demo is strong enough to justify paid T15 later.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 30 tool runs from video links in 14 days.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Welcome email 1 asks which platforms you play
experiments.hypothesis: One-click platform links in welcome email 1 tag ≥ 40% of new members and feed segments [R20 §4].
experiments.change: C42 email 1: 'Where do you play? Click all that apply' (PC, PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, handheld).
experiments.metric: Unique clicks on platform links ÷ delivered
experiments.expected_learning: Whether members will self-segment by email.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 40% of delivered click at least one platform link.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Personalised releases email vs generic list
experiments.hypothesis: 'Your releases this week' (C41) gets ≥ 2× the click rate of the generic release section in The Save File for the same members.
experiments.audience: Members with wishlists or reminders who also subscribe.
experiments.change: Send C41 Mondays from 26 Oct; compare with clicks on the release section of Friday's issue.
experiments.metric: Unique clicks ÷ delivered (alert_clicked for C41)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether personalisation is TechPlay's newsletter advantage [R20].
experiments.success_threshold: C41 click rate ≥ 2× the generic section's, with ≥ 100 delivered on each.

experiments.name: Release-day alert: email vs Discord DM
experiments.hypothesis: For members reachable on both, a Discord DM release alert produces more visits within 24 h than email.
experiments.audience: Members with email and linked Discord who set reminders.
experiments.change: Channel assigned by user id parity for alerts sent from 19 Oct.
experiments.metric: alert_clicked ÷ reminder_delivered, per channel
experiments.expected_learning: Which default channel to set for reminders.
experiments.success_threshold: One channel ≥ 1.3× the other after ≥ 60 deliveries per channel; adopt it as the default.

experiments.name: Price-drop threshold: member-set vs fixed
experiments.hypothesis: Letting members set their own discount threshold raises clicks per alert and lowers unsubscribes.
experiments.change: D-027 with a threshold field vs a fixed 30% default; parity split.
experiments.metric: Clicks per alert; unsubscribes per alert
experiments.expected_learning: How to keep deal alerts useful through Black Friday (C31).
experiments.success_threshold: Member-set arm ≥ 1.2× clicks per alert with unsubscribes not higher than the fixed arm.

experiments.name: Suppress non-clickers after eight sends
experiments.hypothesis: Suppressing subscribers with no click in eight consecutive sends keeps complaints under 0.1% without losing clicks.
experiments.change: Suppression rule in the campaign desk from issue 9.
experiments.metric: Complaint rate per send; total unique clicks per send
experiments.expected_learning: The list-hygiene rule for a self-hosted sender [R20 §4].
experiments.success_threshold: Complaint rate < 0.1% on every send AND total clicks per send down less than 5%.

experiments.name: Plain-text style vs designed template
experiments.hypothesis: A plain, letter-style issue gets more clicks than the designed template.
experiments.change: Alternate template by issue for six issues.
experiments.metric: Unique clicks ÷ delivered
experiments.expected_learning: Whether design effort helps deliverability or clicks.
experiments.success_threshold: Winner ≥ 1.2× click rate across 3 issues each.

experiments.name: Remove share and retweet tasks
experiments.hypothesis: Removing share_giveaway and twitter_retweet tasks (Meta Promotions policy [R16 §2.15]) does not reduce entries by more than 20%.
experiments.change: Next giveaway runs without those tasks; compare with the previous one.
experiments.metric: giveaway_entered per 1,000 giveaway-page sessions
experiments.expected_learning: Whether compliance costs anything; it is required before any paid giveaway promotion.
experiments.success_threshold: Non-inferiority: entry rate ≥ 0.8× the previous giveaway's rate.

experiments.name: One-click entry with Google or Discord
experiments.hypothesis: Making social sign-in the entry step raises entry completion for guests.
experiments.change: Entry button opens social sign-in and enters on return (D-014 redirect).
experiments.metric: giveaway_entered ÷ guest sessions on the giveaway page
experiments.expected_learning: How much of the giveaway drop is registration friction.
experiments.success_threshold: Entry rate ≥ 1.5× the previous giveaway's guest entry rate.

experiments.name: Import prompt after entry
experiments.hypothesis: After entry, 'Connect Steam and your library is ready when the draw closes' (no extra entries offered) raises entrants' A2.
experiments.change: Post-entry panel with Steam/Xbox connect buttons (25-GIVEAWAYS SHELVE stage).
experiments.metric: library_connected within 7 days ÷ giveaway_entered (first entries); giveaway-only share
experiments.expected_learning: Whether giveaway accounts can become real members.
experiments.success_threshold: Entrant→A2 ≥ 25% AND giveaway-only share at close ≤ 60% (guardrail in 25-GIVEAWAYS).
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Daily check-in with a weekly freeze
experiments.hypothesis: Adding one freeze per week to the giveaway check-in streak keeps entrants returning without punishing a missed day [R12].
experiments.change: Streak freeze on the daily bonus in the next giveaway.
experiments.metric: Distinct return days per entrant; share of streak-breakers who never return
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a humane streak retains as well as a strict one.
experiments.success_threshold: Median return days ≥ 1.3× the previous giveaway AND the never-return share among streak-breakers falls.

experiments.name: Giveaway hub indexable while live
experiments.hypothesis: Making /giveaways indexable while a draw is open brings organic entrants [R01].
experiments.change: D-039 index while live, canonical on giveaway pages.
experiments.metric: Organic sessions to /giveaways and /giveaway/* during the live window
experiments.expected_learning: Whether giveaways can be found without paid or social push.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 20 organic sessions/week by week 3 of a live giveaway.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: T1 Google branded exact match
experiments.hypothesis: A branded exact-match campaign costs almost nothing and shows whether anyone bids on 'techplay' [R16 T1].
experiments.audience: Searchers typing techplay, techplay gg, techplay wow analyzer, techplay backlog advisor.
experiments.change: C56 from 19 Oct: 2 RSAs, sitelinks to /games, /wow-analyzer, /backlog-advisor; $60–90/month.
experiments.metric: Impression share, CPC, sessions with utm_medium=cpc
experiments.expected_learning: The real branded CPC and whether the brand has any search demand.
experiments.success_threshold: Keep if CPC ≤ $1.00 and ≥ 10 impressions/week after 14 days; otherwise pause (R16 stop-loss).

experiments.name: T2 Meta library-import demo
experiments.hypothesis: A 6–15 s screen recording of the Steam/Xbox/PSN import converts US adults to verified accounts more cheaply than a content ad [R16 T2].
experiments.change: C57 (2–22 Nov): Leads/registration objective, on-site event via CAPI, three creatives.
experiments.metric: Cost per email_verified; cost per A2
experiments.expected_learning: A first readable cost per verified registration.
experiments.success_threshold: Continue if ≤ $10 per verified registration; stop at $150 spent with < 5 verified accounts.

experiments.name: T3 GTA 6 hub carousel vs generic creative
experiments.hypothesis: Cards for the map, vehicles and characters out-click a generic 'gaming news' creative [R16 T3].
experiments.change: Carousel creative in C57, each card deep-linked with its own utm_content.
experiments.metric: CTR; cost per registration_complete
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the GTA 6 hub is TechPlay's best paid hook before 19 Nov.
experiments.success_threshold: Keep if CTR ≥ 1% at 5,000 impressions; stop below 1%.

experiments.name: T4 Reddit Conversation Placement to Discord
experiments.hypothesis: Ads in GTA 6 threads drive Discord joins at under $3 each [R16 T4].
experiments.change: C58 (9–25 Nov): post-style ad ('1,058 GTA 6 locations on one free map, and a Discord for launch week.'); map wording cleared under D-020, own invite code.
experiments.metric: Cost per discord_click; discord_join by invite code
experiments.expected_learning: Paid cost of a community member.
experiments.success_threshold: Continue if cost per attributed join ≤ $3; stop at $100 with < 20 Discord clicks.

experiments.name: T5 WoW Analyzer tool ad on Reddit
experiments.hypothesis: A tool ad in WoW subreddits beats any article ad on tool runs per dollar [R16 T5].
experiments.change: C58 ad set: screenshot of an analysis result, 'Paste your character'.
experiments.metric: tool_run (tool=wow) per $; registration_complete
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a niche tool can be bought cheaply.
experiments.success_threshold: Continue if ≥ 30 analyses per $100; stop at $100 with < 30 analyses or if Groq cost exceeds ad cost.

experiments.name: T6 Backlog Advisor on Reddit
experiments.hypothesis: Backlog Advisor resonates with 'too many games' communities [R16 T6].
experiments.change: Screen tour of the advisor output; lands on guest mode (D-037).
experiments.metric: tool_run (tool=backlog) → library_connected
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the backlog problem is a paid acquisition hook.
experiments.success_threshold: Stop if CTR < 0.2%; continue if ≥ 10% of tool runs import a library.

experiments.name: T7 Tool exact-match search
experiments.hypothesis: Exact-match tool queries ('wow raid readiness', 'what should I play next', 'backlog tool') have real volume [R16 T7].
experiments.change: Second ad group in C56 once T1 is stable.
experiments.metric: Impressions/week, CPC, tool_run
experiments.expected_learning: Search demand for TechPlay's tools, which no research could size [R03].
experiments.success_threshold: Stop if < 20 impressions/week after 14 days.

experiments.name: T8 TikTok Spark boost
experiments.hypothesis: Boosting an organic GTA 6 map video that already performs reaches under $6 CPM [R16 T8].
experiments.change: Only at the AGGRESSIVE budget and only if an organic video beat the median by 3×.
experiments.metric: CPM; utm sessions in the first-party counter; registration_complete
experiments.expected_learning: Whether paid video amplification is worth the $50/day floor.
experiments.success_threshold: Stop at $350 if CPM > $10 or 0 registrations.

experiments.name: T9 Meta newsletter double opt-in
experiments.hypothesis: Newsletter double opt-in from ads costs less than $8 per verified subscriber [R16 T9].
experiments.change: C57 second ad set to /newsletter with the 'weekly releases, one fix, one number' promise.
experiments.metric: Cost per newsletter_verified
experiments.expected_learning: Whether email is cheaper to buy than accounts.
experiments.success_threshold: Continue if ≤ $8 per verified subscriber; stop at $100 with 0 verified.

experiments.name: T10 Meta retargeting of registration starters
experiments.hypothesis: Retargeting people who started registration recovers 10% of them [R16 T10].
experiments.audience: Pixel audience: visited /register or the wizard in 7 days, no registration.
experiments.change: Only if the pool reaches 500 within 30 days.
experiments.metric: Cost per registration_complete; recovered share
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a small-site retargeting pool is usable at all.
experiments.success_threshold: Skip if pool < 500 after 30 days; continue if ≥ 10% of the pool recovers at ≤ $10 each.

experiments.name: T11 Free Discord listings
experiments.hypothesis: Disboard and Discadia listings deliver measurable joins at no cost [R16 T11].
experiments.audience: Discord users browsing tags (gta6, wow, pc).
experiments.change: SC lists the server with one invite code per listing.
experiments.metric: discord_join per week by invite code; 7-day posting rate of those joiners
experiments.expected_learning: A zero-cost baseline for Discord acquisition.
experiments.success_threshold: Keep if ≥ 5 joins/week sustained over 4 weeks and ≥ 30% post within 7 days; drop if 0 joins in 4 weeks.

experiments.name: T12 Paid newsletter swap
experiments.hypothesis: A paid swap with one gaming newsletter beats Meta on cost per verified subscriber [R16 T12].
experiments.change: One dedicated blurb with UTM; only once TechPlay's own list size is known and can be stated honestly.
experiments.metric: Cost per newsletter_verified
experiments.expected_learning: Whether newsletter-to-newsletter is a viable channel for a self-hosted list.
experiments.success_threshold: Run only after the list size is known; succeed if cost per verified < the X-084 result.

experiments.name: T13 Giveaway ads
experiments.hypothesis: Giveaway ads pull entrants who also connect a library [R16 T13].
experiments.change: Only after X-071 (no share tasks) and legal review of no-purchase-necessary and AMOE [R16 §2.15].
experiments.metric: Entrants with library_connected within 7 days; giveaway-only share
experiments.expected_learning: Whether paid giveaway traffic creates members or only entries.
experiments.success_threshold: Stop if > 70% of paid entrants have zero other activity (R16 T13 hard stop).

experiments.name: T14 Web push opt-in on GTA 6 reminders
experiments.hypothesis: Push opt-in offered only after 'Notify me' on GTA 6 pages builds a re-engagement list for free [R16 T14; spine C59].
experiments.audience: GTA 6 hub and release-time tool users.
experiments.change: C59 prompt only after the user clicks 'Notify me'; never on page load (Chrome demotes low-acceptance sites [R07]).
experiments.metric: notification_enabled ÷ /gta6* sessions; click rate on the first push
experiments.expected_learning: Whether push is worth keeping after launch week.
experiments.success_threshold: Keep if opt-in ≥ 1% of hub sessions after 2 weeks and first-push click rate ≥ 5%; stop below 1%.

experiments.name: T15 YouTube Shorts ad for the WoW demo
experiments.hypothesis: Shorts CPM is cheap enough for a 15-second Analyzer demo [R16 T15].
experiments.change: Parked for Q4: the spine excludes Demand Gen (§12). Revisit in Q1 2027 as a video-views buy only if X-064 succeeds.
experiments.metric: CPM, view rate, tool_run
experiments.expected_learning: Whether paid Shorts can feed a niche tool.
experiments.success_threshold: Stop if CPM > $8 or 0 tool runs after $150.

experiments.name: GTA 6 release-time tool with reminder
experiments.hypothesis: A tool that shows the unlock time in the visitor's time zone and offers 'remind me at pre-load and unlock' gets reminder_set from ≥ 10% of users [R17].
experiments.change: D-018 /gta6/release-time (new), C08; reminder through D-016.
experiments.metric: reminder_set ÷ tool_run (tool=release-time)
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a utility tool converts better than content before a launch.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 10% of tool users set a reminder AND ≥ 200 reminders by 18 Nov.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Calendar export (ICS) and return visits
experiments.hypothesis: Members who export their wishlist calendar return more, because each calendar entry links back with from=ics.
experiments.change: D-036 ICS export; event descriptions link to the game page with from=ics (internal marker, no UTM).
experiments.metric: Sessions with from=ics; D30 retention of exporters vs matched non-exporters
experiments.expected_learning: Whether a calendar entry is a retention channel.
experiments.success_threshold: Exporters' D30 retention ≥ 1.5× matched non-exporters, with ≥ 20 exporters.

experiments.name: GTA 6 map tracker: save progress with an account
experiments.hypothesis: Letting guests tick locations and asking for an account only to save progress converts ≥ 5% of tracker users.
experiments.change: C11 tracker in guest mode; 'Save your progress' opens the D-016 modal.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (from=gta6) ÷ guest tool users
experiments.expected_learning: Whether launch-week utility is the best registration moment of the quarter.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 5% of guest users register, with ≥ 200 guest users in launch week.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Game Awards prediction league
experiments.hypothesis: A free prediction league for 10 Dec brings new registrations and a reason to return on the night.
experiments.audience: S10 Community Regulars, S8, awards followers.
experiments.change: C29 / D-026 league with a public leaderboard; entry needs an account.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (from=predictions); entries; returns on 10–11 Dec
experiments.expected_learning: Whether event-driven games create accounts that stay.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 100 entries AND ≥ 25 new registrations from the league AND ≥ 50% of entrants return on 10–11 Dec.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Your 2026 in Games
experiments.hypothesis: A cross-platform year in review produces shares that bring registrations.
experiments.change: C28 / D-025 live 14–31 Dec with a share card (D-024).
experiments.metric: share_card_generated (type=yir) ÷ members viewing; registration_complete with utm_campaign=c28-your-2026
experiments.expected_learning: Whether the library can market itself once a year.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 25% of eligible members generate a card AND ≥ 1 registration per 10 shares.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)

experiments.name: Taste Match invite link
experiments.hypothesis: A 'compare your taste with me' link brings verified accounts and makes the unreachable 'Squad Goals' achievement reachable [R11 §3].
experiments.audience: Members and the people they invite.
experiments.change: Invite link on the profile and Gamer DNA card; landing shows a blurred match until sign-up.
experiments.metric: registration_complete (from=profile) ÷ invite-link visitors
experiments.expected_learning: Whether member-to-member invites work at TechPlay's size.
experiments.success_threshold: ≥ 10% of invite visitors register AND ≥ 10 registrations in 28 days.
experiments.design: absolute threshold, no control (volume too small)
